## EMST role: Hydrologist (state variant, lead level; P2)

*Match:* `skos:closeMatch`, agentConfidence (uncalibrated) 0.55, unreviewed agent candidate (not reviewed by a person) (`emst-x5-tx:R17-hydrologist/state:2466`). *Authority position (editorial):* resource-manager.

**Competency targets at this level (editorial draft target levels, agent-drafted)**

- Plan water supply and allocation under hydrologic uncertainty — lead L4
- Characterize groundwater systems and protect drinking water sources — lead L4
- Assess stream channel form and function in the field — lead L3
- Measure water quality and survey aquatic communities in the field — lead L3
- Build, calibrate and validate predictive and simulation models of environmental systems — lead L4
- Quantify and communicate uncertainty for environmental decisions — lead L3
- Analyze environmental data statistically and interpret the results — lead L3
- Deploy, maintain and verify field sensor networks — lead L3
- Develop pollutant load allocations and watershed restoration plans for impaired waters — lead L3
- Analyze and interpret climate observations and projections for management decisions — lead L3
- Evaluate model fitness-for-purpose and validate against independent evidence — lead L3
- Interpret and question environmental data products in everyday work — lead L1
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — lead L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — lead L1
- Record provenance and AI involvement in work products — lead L1

**Main tasks at this level (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- Forecast water demand and supply under drought and climate scenarios for a utility or basin plan, stating assumptions and uncertainty
- Prepare a drought contingency plan with triggers, stages and response actions tied to supply indicators
- Evaluate a water-right or allocation application against water availability, priority and impairment of existing users
- Compare conjunctive-use, reuse and storage options by yield, cost and reliability for an integrated resource plan
- Run an aquifer test on a supply well or wellfield to estimate transmissivity and storage from drawdown and recovery data
- Delineate a wellhead or source-water protection area from hydrogeologic data and time-of-travel criteria
- Review a well construction or injection well application against construction and protection standards before approval
- Evaluate contaminant transport toward a supply well from monitoring data and a groundwater model, recommending protective actions
- Simulate ecosystem response to alternative land-use and climate scenarios, documenting scenario assumptions and the sensitivity of results to each.
- Present model outputs to stakeholders for an adaptive management decision, stating the conditions under which the projections should not be trusted.
- Build a predictive model of fire risk, pest outbreak or water availability, validating it on years or areas withheld from fitting.
- Forecast resource management needs from a validated predictive model, stating the horizon and interval for each estimate.
